title: YouTube star Cliff Tan apologises to 2.4 million fans after promoting an AI design tool
excerpt: Cliff Tan apologised to 2.4 million subscribers for a paid Dreamina ad, the second YouTube creator in a week to walk back an AI association.
content_html:
Interior design creator Cliff Tan has apologised to his 2.4 million YouTube subscribers for a paid advertisement for Dreamina, ByteDance’s AI creative tool. It is the second creator apology in a week, after Hank Green walked back his use of ChatGPT for research.

An interior design creator with 2.4 million YouTube subscribers has apologised for running an AI advertisement. Cliff Tan, who posts as Dear Modern, published a video on Monday walking the sponsorship back. “Yesterday I made a video on AI, and it disappointed many of you,” he said. “I’m really sorry about that.”

The ad was for Dreamina, an AI tool that turns written prompts into animated video. Tan uploaded his own hand-drawn sketches and had the software animate them into a floor plan.

He had tried to inoculate himself inside the ad itself, saying he does not “like AI” because “it makes you forget to use your brain.” It made no difference. The comments filled with objections, one of them collecting 1,700 likes: “No, Mr. Cliff. Please. Don’t sell yourself to AI.”

In a follow-up comment Tan said he had thought the software “would be genuinely useful to fellow designers.” He added that he did not want viewers “with the right sentiments, to be martyrs in a world that is increasingly leaving us behind.”

Part of the anger was aimed at the advertiser. Dreamina is CapCut’s AI brand and belongs to ByteDance, and it runs on the Seedance models the company recently fitted with watermarking and IP guardrails before a global rollout.

This is the second apology of its kind in a week. Hank Green, who has more than 3.2 million subscribers, apologised on August 4 for leaning on ChatGPT to find papers and sources for his scripts, and afterwards published a personal AI policy ruling out letting a model write, edit or outline anything.

Neither creator generated content wholesale. Both were punished for the association, which is the part worth noting for anyone selling AI tools through influencers. It is a rougher market than the sponsorship rates suggest, on a platform already punishing human creators caught in its slop crackdown.

The profession Tan works in has been drifting the other way. The British Institute of Interior Design said last year that AI “has a growing presence in interior design,” with firm founder Stephen Dick telling it that “the possibilities are impressive” with text-to-image visualisation tools.

content_html_zh:
室内设计创作者 Cliff Tan 就字节跳动人工智能创意工具 Dreamina 的付费广告向他的 240 万 YouTube 订阅者道歉。 这是汉克·格林 (Hank Green) 放弃使用 ChatGPT 进行研究后，一周内第二次向创作者道歉。

一位拥有 240 万 YouTube 订阅者的室内设计创作者为投放人工智能广告而道歉。 克里夫·谭（Cliff Tan）以“亲爱的摩登”（Dear Modern）的名义发布了一段视频，周一发布了一段视频，要求收回赞助。 “昨天我制作了一段关于人工智能的视频，这让你们很多人感到失望，”他说。 “对此我真的很抱歉。”

该广告是针对 Dreamina 的，这是一种人工智能工具，可以将书面提示转换为动画视频。 谭上传了自己的手绘草图，并让软件将它们动画化为平面图。

他曾试图在广告本身中表达自己的观点，称他不“喜欢人工智能”，因为“它会让你忘记使用你的大脑”。 这没有什么区别。 评论中充满了反对意见，其中一条获得了 1,700 个赞：“不，克里夫先生。 请。 不要把自己卖给人工智能。”

谭在后续评论中表示，他认为该软件“对其他设计师来说确实有用”。 他补充说，他不希望观众“在一个越来越把我们抛在后面的世界中，怀着正确的情感成为烈士”。

部分愤怒是针对广告商的。 Dreamina 是 CapCut 的人工智能品牌，隶属于字节跳动，它运行在 Seedance 模型上，该公司最近在全球推出之前安装了水印和 IP 护栏。

这是一周内第二次此类道歉。 拥有超过 320 万订阅者的汉克·格林 (Hank Green) 于 8 月 4 日为依靠 ChatGPT 寻找其脚本的论文和来源而道歉，并随后发布了一项个人人工智能政策，禁止模型编写、编辑或概述任何内容。

两位创作者都批量生产内容。 两人都因该协会受到了惩罚，对于任何通过影响者销售人工智能工具的人来说，这是值得注意的部分。 这是一个比赞助费所显示的更为严峻的市场，在这个平台上，已经在惩罚陷入腐败打击的人类创作者。

谭所从事的职业却在朝着相反的方向发展。 英国室内设计学会去年表示，人工智能“在室内设计领域的应用越来越广泛”，公司创始人斯蒂芬·迪克表示，文本到图像可视化工具的“可能性令人印象深刻”。
